components.description: The university's Family and Medical Leave Policy (Blue Book Appendix IV), which restates the federal FMLA: up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a 12-month period for a birth, placement for adoption or foster care, care of a seriously ill child, spouse or parent, or the employee's own serious health condition.
components.mechanism_note: The policy restates the FMLA without adding length, so it is coded as the statute (schema statute_source; U2, U4).
components.faculty_group_note: All full-time and part-time faculty, administrative/professional and hourly staff employees who have been employed for at least one year, and for a minimum of 1,250 hours over the previous twelve months.
components.eligible_parent_wording: upon the birth of the employee's child; upon the placement of a child with the employee for adoption or foster care; to care for a child, spouse, or parent; the employee's own serious health condition
components.service_requirement: employed for at least one year, and for a minimum of 1,250 hours over the previous twelve months
components.dual_employee_rule: Spouses who are both employed by the university are entitled to a combined total of twelve weeks of leave (rather than twelve weeks each) for the birth or placement
components.entitlement_note: Statutory entitlement (FMLA); the approval steps in the procedures are notice and arrangements (U2; schema).
components.duration_note: Up to twelve weeks per 12-month period; the statute states 12 workweeks. Intermittent or reduced-schedule leave for a birth or adoption if agreed by the supervisor, dean and Director of Personnel Services. Paid time off counts toward the twelve-week maximum.
components.medical_certification_note: For leave due to illness (the employee's own or a family member's): medical certification of commencement date, approximate return, medical facts and, for own illness, inability to perform the job; a physician's statement of fitness to return. No certification stated for leave upon a birth or placement.
components.time_window: within one (1) year of the birth or placement of a child
components.notice: reasonable prior notice (thirty (30) days in advance of the effective date of leave, if possible)
components.relief_note: A leave of absence with no relief stated (R9).

notes: 2018_02 differs from 2018_01 (revised collegiate criteria for Business and Law, a new Law resident-contract guideline and Oxley College of Health Sciences criteria); Statement Section X and Appendices III and IV are textually identical in both. 2018_01 (captured 2015) is cited first; the Statement is fixed by its 2004 revisions and Appendix IV is effective June 1, 1994; both are read as in force on 2018-02-26 per their version notes.

What the sources contain: 2018_01/02 are the faculty Statement on Academic Freedom, Responsibility, and Tenure (part of the employment contract, I.A, II.A) with Section X Faculty Leaves (X.A general leave of absence, X.C family and sick leave and a one-year term-appointment extension) and Appendix IV, the university's Family and Medical Leave Policy, which covers all faculty. 2018_00 is an undated HR benefits summary (copy from 2015) listing long-term disability for full-time faculty; its vacation and sick-leave entries cover administrative/professional and hourly staff only. A governing document for faculty leave is therefore saved (the no-policy coding (`missing`) not triggered): missing = false.

No paid parental, maternity or childbirth leave and no modified-duties policy for new parents appears in any saved source. Childbirth is handled as FMLA leave (c1), with pay only from the employee's own sick leave, vacation and floating holiday (c2), and a discretionary medical leave beyond 12 weeks while medically necessary (c3).

Documents cited but not saved: the University's sick leave policies (Statement X.C; the faculty sick-leave accrual and amount are therefore unknown); the Personal Leave Policy (Appendix IV item 19; up to 40 additional weeks of unpaid leave, coded c7 from the reference alone); Court Leave/Jury Duty policy (Appendix IV note; not a parental provision); 'current University fringe benefit, research, personnel and other applicable policies' (II.A); the long-term disability plan document (Prudential); the University Bylaws (I.D); the College of Law 'Guidelines Governing Resident Contract Faculty' (saved inside 2018_02). Statement X.B's reference to 'Appendix IV.1' for sabbaticals points to Appendix III.

Not components: sabbatical leave (Appendix III; for scholarly renewal, cannot be taken for a birth); court leave/jury duty; administrative stays of tenure or post-tenure review for faculty holding administrative posts (IV.B, V.B); extraordinary extension of the probationary period for exceptional promise (IV.B.2-3); dismissal for medical reasons (VII.D); hourly-staff sick leave and A/P and hourly vacation (benefits page; not faculty).

FMLA restoration exception (Appendix IV item 15): an exempt employee among the highest-paid 10% may be denied restoration if it would cause substantial and grievous economic injury; recorded here, not coded.

Chain, birth parent: FMLA leave 12 weeks (c1), paid only from own sick leave then vacation within it (c2) -> medical leave beyond 12 weeks while medically necessary (c3, discretionary, no stated length) and/or Personal Leave extension up to 40 weeks (c7, discretionary, policy not saved), each consecutive_after c1; long-term disability (c4) may begin after six months of total disability.

Chain, non-birth parent: FMLA leave 12 weeks (c1), own balances within it only where a physician certifies bonding time as medically necessary (c2) -> Personal Leave extension up to 40 weeks (c7, discretionary), consecutive_after c1.

General-purpose provisions recorded but counted in no figure (U1): c5 one-year term/tenure-clock extension (personal emergency, ill health, family responsibilities; discretionary); c6 general leave of absence (president's decision); c8 dean's discretionary one-semester teaching excusal stated in the sabbatical eligibility clause.
